{{nihongo|'''Nyuukawa Shrine (Uchi district)'''|丹生川神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

**Nyūkawa Shrine** (にゅうかわじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Nyūkawa-chō (formerly {{ill|Ōno District, Gifu|Q31671|qid=Q31671}}{{ill|Nyūkawa, Gifu|Q7071339|qid=Q7071339|lt=Nyūkawa Village}}), {{ill|Takayama, Gifu|Q622594|qid=Q622594}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}.

The shrine’s name is derived from {{ill|Nyūkawa, Gifu|Q7071339|qid=Q7071339|lt=Nyūkawa Village}} in {{ill|Ōno District, Gifu|Q31671|qid=Q31671}} and has no direct relation to {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}’s {{ill|Niukawakami Shrine (Q246370)|Q246370|qid=Q246370}}, {{ill|Niukawakami Upper Shrine|Q10877366|qid=Q10877366}}, or {{ill|Niukawakami Lower Shrine|Q10877367|qid=Q10877367}}.

== Overview ==
Originally, it was Yakama Shrine, enshrined in the Bokata district of Nyūkawa Village. During the shrine consolidation policy ({{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700}}) in the late Meiji period, several shrines within the village were merged, and it was renamed **Nyūkawa Shrine**.

The date of establishment is unknown. In the past, it was known as “Yasō no Mori” and “Hachimen Aragū-gū” {{Sfn|Tsuchida|1987|p=43}}.

In {{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}} (Meiji 1), it was renamed Yakama Shrine {{Sfn|Tsuchida|1987|p=43}}. In {{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}} (Meiji 4), it became a village shrine.

In {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} (Meiji 40), Kumano Shrine and Kifune Shrine were merged into it. At the same time, an application was submitted to Gifu Prefecture to change the name from Yakama Shrine to Nyūkawa Shrine, which was approved the following year {{Sfn|Nyūkawa Village History|2000|p=436}}. In {{ill|1913|Q2080|qid=Q2080}} (Taishō 2), Kumano Shrine was merged. In {{ill|1914|Q2083|qid=Q2083}} (Taishō 3), it was officially renamed **Nyūkawa Shrine** {{Sfn|Tsuchida|1987|p=44}}.

Thereafter, through the early Shōwa period, shrines within Nyūkawa Village (including Shinmei Shrine, Kumano Shrine, Suwa Shrine, and Bijoshima Shrine) were successively merged {{Sfn|Tsuchida|1987|p=44}}. As repeated mergers made the precincts cramped, the grounds were expanded and improved in {{ill|1952|Q5272|qid=Q5272}} (Shōwa 27), and a new main hall and other buildings were constructed {{Sfn|Tsuchida|1987|p=44}}. In the same year, Hakusan Shrine was merged.

In {{ill|1956|Q5221|qid=Q5221}} (Shōwa 31), it was designated a {{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592|lt=Ginpeisha}} by the Gifu Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines {{Sfn|Tsuchida|1987|p=44}}.
